identity.title: The Molecular Gas in the NGC 6240 Merging Galaxy System at the Highest Spatial Resolution

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the highest resolution — 15 pc (0.03”) — ALMA $^{12}$CO(2-1) line emission and 1.3mm continuum maps, tracers of the molecular gas and dust, respectively, in the nearby merging galaxy system NGC 6240

evidence.quote: For our work, the nuclear positions were obtained from the Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations of this source, as reported by (cite: hagiwara11).
For our work, the nuclear positions were obtained from the Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations of this source, as reported by (cite: hagiwara11).

question.value: How is the molecular gas distributed and moving at 15 pc resolution in the NGC 6240 dual-AGN merger, and how much gas is available to feed each SMBH or drive outflows?

evidence.quote: We are thus directly imaging the reservoir of gas that can accrete onto each supermassive black hole.
ALMA observed NGC 6240 as part of its cycle 3 program 2015.1.00370.S (PI: E. Treister).
Data from program 2015.1.00003.S (cite: saito18) were also included to improve the recovery of the large scale structure from intermediate-length baselines.
the high resolution band 6 ALMA observations of the $^{12}$CO(2-1) emission

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs of 1875 MHz (7.5 GHz total), 1.953 MHz resolution; CO(2-1) SPW centered at 225.1 GHz; continuum SPWs at 227.5, 239.9, 241.9 GHz

evidence.quote: The total ALMA bandwidth of 7.5 GHz was divided into four spectral windows (SPWs) of 1875 MHz each and a spectral resolution of 1.953 MHz.
The remaining ones were used to trace the mm continuum centered at frequencies of 227.5 GHz, 239.9 GHz and 241.9 GHz
The $^{12}$CO(2-1) at rest-frame 230.538 GHz was targeted as a tracer of the molecular gas

baselines.value: 15 m to 15 km, three array configurations

evidence.quote: recovering most of the total flux at large scales by combining three different array configurations (baselines from 15 meters to 15 km)
The achieved angular resolution is $\sim$0.03$''$, corresponding to a physical scale of $\sim$15 pc
we are able to recover all the emission out to scales of 30$''$

sensitivity.value: Cube RMS ~0.28 mJy/beam; continuum RMS 0.024 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: The final RMS of the cube is $\sim$0.28 mJy/beam.
the RMS of the final image is 0.024 mJy/beam
the optical imaging provided by the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) using the Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 (WFPC2) instrument

what.value: Nuclear positions and SMBH sphere-of-influence radii (235 and 212 pc)

evidence.quote: radii of 235$\pm$8 pc and 212$\pm$9 pc for the northern and southern nuclei, respectively

pipeline_or_manual.value: Standard ALMA reduction with modifications; WVR scaling, step-wise self-calibration

evidence.quote: In general, the standard ALMA data reduction[^1] approach was pursued, with some specific differences.

evidence.quote: J1751$+$0939 was used as flux calibrator instead of Pallas, which showed problematic amplitude visibilities

self_calibration.value: Compact/intermediate: single phase-only step, solint inf. Long baseline: unfolding self-cal with baseline cuts 800, 2400, 4000, 8000 klambda, >=3 baselines, >1.5 sigma, gaintype T, per scan

evidence.quote: a single self-calibration step considering phase solutions alone was adopted
Such step-wise (“unfolding”) approach was considered using the following baseline cuts: 800, 2400, 4000, 8000 k$\lambda$.
This was done using a natural weighting scheme that led to a beam size on the $^{12}$CO(2-1) line cube of 0.06$''$$\times$0.032$''$

evidence.quote: the use of feathering on a per-channel basis, when retrieving the $^{12}$CO(2-1) emission map, prevented this low-surface density to be parsed to the final combined map.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting and per-channel feathering to keep line fluxes reliable despite long-baseline decorrelation

evidence.quote: Similarly, by comparing with previously reported $^{12}$CO(2-1) fluxes at a range of scales and resolutions we concluded that our line measurements have not been significantly affected.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Long-baseline EB Xac5575/X8a5f excluded due to poor phase stability

evidence.quote: the final images consider the Xc5148b/X127e alone, which is less affected by signal decorrelation

limitations_admitted.value: Continuum fluxes at ~1'' scales biased by decorrelation and sparse uv coverage; dust-based masses biased low
